orc-3109-04.name: Allocation of parental rights and shared parenting
orc-3109-04.summary: How Ohio courts allocate parental rights and responsibilities (custody), approve shared parenting plans, and weigh the best-interest factors in division (F)(1).

orc-3109-042.name: Unmarried mother as default custodian
orc-3109-042.summary: Under ORC 3109.042, an unmarried mother is the sole residential parent and legal custodian until a court orders otherwise. What that default means for both parents.

orc-3109-051.name: Parenting time and companionship
orc-3109-051.summary: Ohio's statute on parenting time for parents and companionship or visitation for relatives, including the factors courts weigh in setting schedules.

orc-3109-11.name: Relatives' visitation after a parent's death
orc-3109-11.summary: When a parent has died, ORC 3109.11 lets that parent's relatives, including grandparents, ask a court for reasonable companionship or visitation with the child.

orc-3109-12.name: Relatives' visitation when parents were unmarried
orc-3109-12.summary: ORC 3109.12 covers companionship or visitation for grandparents and other relatives of a child born to an unmarried mother.

orc-chapter-3119.name: Child support calculation and modification
orc-chapter-3119.summary: Ohio's child support chapter: the guideline worksheet, income definitions, imputed income, deviations, and how a support order is reviewed or modified.

orc-chapter-3127.name: Interstate custody jurisdiction (UCCJEA)
orc-chapter-3127.summary: Ohio's version of the Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement Act: which state's court can decide custody and visitation, the six-month home-state rule, continuing jurisdiction after a move, and enforcing out-of-state orders.

orc-2919-21.name: Nonsupport of dependents
orc-2919-21.summary: ORC 2919.21 makes certain failures to provide support a crime, separate from civil child support enforcement by the county CSEA.

orc-2919-23.name: Interference with custody
orc-2919-23.summary: What counts as interference with custody in Ohio under ORC 2919.23, and why the exchange times in a parenting order matter.

orc-3113-31.name: Domestic violence civil protection orders
orc-3113-31.summary: How Ohio domestic violence civil protection orders work under ORC 3113.31: emergency ex parte orders, the full hearing, and what an order can require.

orc-149-43.name: Ohio Public Records Act
orc-149-43.summary: Ohio's Public Records Act, ORC 149.43: how to request records from public offices. Access to court case records is also governed by Sup.R. 44–47.

orc-2317-02.name: Privileged communications
orc-2317-02.summary: ORC 2317.02 lists communications that generally cannot be compelled as testimony, including those with physicians and licensed counselors. How the privilege applies when mental health is raised in a custody case is contested. Confirm with an attorney.

sup-r-48.name: Guardians ad litem
sup-r-48.summary: The Ohio Rules of Superintendence on guardians ad litem (Sup.R. 48 and its subparts): appointment, training, duties, reports, and complaints.
